test.explain: Three separate test binaries run in sequence: unit tests compiled from src/ with cfg(test), each file in tests/ as its own crate, and finally every code block in your doc comments. Tests inside one binary run in parallel threads.

clippy.explain: Clippy runs the compiler front end plus hundreds of extra lints grouped by category (style, correctness, complexity, perf, pedantic). Most come with a machine-applicable fix: cargo clippy --fix. In CI, -- -D warnings turns warnings into errors.

fmt.explain: --check does not modify files: it prints a diff and exits with status 1, which is exactly what you want in CI. Locally, plain cargo fmt rewrites the files. There is one canonical style, so formatting is never a code-review topic.

doc.explain: rustdoc renders your /// comments (Markdown) into a static HTML site, with cross links to your dependencies' docs. The same tool powers docs.rs, where every crate published on crates.io gets its documentation built automatically.

release.explain: The release profile enables opt-level = 3, removes debug assertions and integer overflow checks, and writes to target/release/. It is slower to compile, often much faster to run: never benchmark a debug build.
